title: Seishun Buta Yarou wa Randoseru Girl no Yume wo Minai
content:
Cloverworks doubles down on the Demon Slayer formula again. I feel like that’s a pattern we should not ignore anymore, for better of worse.

Sakuta finds himself again, having to deal with yet another traumatic journey, or rather, self-healing one just after he thinks everything has got back to normal. I mean, so we thought.

After last movie established the reform of Kaede, her having to come to terms with her past trauma and Sakuta feeling like he finally hell together just strong enough to see his sister well and happy, comes this movie, keeping it family centered, but this time revolving around the untold closeted struggleof Sakuta himself. Something he has kept buried throughout the show, even to himself and the audience.

If it had ever crossed your mind questioning the the standing between Sakuta and his mother. This movie is about addressing that. It’s weird because before this, you’d think with Kaede finally drawing a genuine smile, everyone in the show has gotten closure and there was nothing left untangled. But after watching this one it really feels like it is. Unless the dad comes in clutch with a something new and troubling, but it’s unlikely. It really makes you think where the story is gonna take us next with the stakes being too low right now. It genuinely feels like a Disney happy ending. But it might just be the eerie quite before the storm.

This and the last movie feel like sibling releases more than anything. They might as well have been a 10 episodes season or one 2 hours long movie. The play well with each other, the share the same themes and familial focus and the continuity is seamless.

Overall: 8/10.
